gholam.text:
رفیق، سم آلتمن توی مصاحبه با مجله تایم حسابی سر و صدا به پا کرده و گفته اوپن‌ای‌آی تا آخر همین سال ۲۰۲۶ بالاخره به یه سیستم داخلی می‌رسه که رسماً میشه اسمشو هوش عمومی مصنوعی یا همون AGI گذاشت. جالب‌تر اینه که این غول فناوری همین حالا هم مدلی به اسم GPT Astra توی آزمایشگاهش داره که عین یه پژوهشگر خودکار، آزمایش‌های علمی رو توی کدهای خودشون پیاده می‌کنه و کار یک‌هفته‌ای یه محقق خبره رو روی هوا تحویل میده. به قول آلتمن، این اولین سیستمی خواهد بود که صرفاً پردازشگر نیست، بلکه قراره خودش دست به کشف دانش و اختراع چیزهای کاملاً جدید بزنه.

اهمیتش اینه که با رسیدن به پژوهشگرهای خودکار و AGI، سرعت پیشرفت کل علم و فناوری دنیا چندین برابر میشه و بازی خلق دانش برای همیشه دستخوش تغییر اساسی خواهد شد.

links.text:
OpenAI officially expects AGI by end of *this* year (2026)

"Altman told me that OpenAI was “not quite yet” there, but that by the end of the year the company would have an internal system he would call AGI."

We did it friends.

And: OpenAI has already internally built autonomous AI researchersbased on its benchmarks. It's the well-known GPT Astra.

"Pachocki says the company has already met its internal benchmark for an automated AI research intern. Given an experimental idea, he says, Astra can implement it inside OpenAI’s code base, run the experiment, and return results, or take a paper and perform work that previously occupied a human researcher for a week."

Astra will have the biggest impact on knowledgework there is

"Astra would enable “persistent agents,” he explained—virtual colleagues toiling for sustained periods on tasks. But its biggest impact, he predicted, would come from people using it to discover new knowledge. “I expect this will be the first model where the model actually invents new things in a way that matters,” Altman told the group. “That’s a very AGI-like thing.”

We did it friends. The finishing line is within sight. This year will be the turning point. Forever.

I am so damn hyped.

quote.text:
TIME’s new cover: In 2026, OpenAI has seen key departures, rogue AI agents, major lawsuits, and has seen increased competition in the AI race. “We clearly had some missteps as a company,” OpenAI CEO Sam Altman tells TIME. 

Inside the company’s plan for a reboot: https://time.com/article/2026/08/26/openai-sam-altman-interview/?utm_source=twitter&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=editorial&utm_content=260826
